title: Live session replay loop and adaptive retry fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers reported sustained 5xx spikes and long streaming timeouts during live inference sessions (webhooks and multipart streaming). Root cause appears to be replayed request batches combined with non-deterministic idempotency key generation in the SDK + cross-mode fallback to Dedicated. This ticket tracks a short-term mitigation (adaptive retry suppression + per-tenant soft-quarantine) and the longer-term fix (normalize idempotency headers + session affinity guard).
steps_to_repro: 1) Start long-lived streaming inference session from SDK v1.x with multipart chunked upload enabled.
2) Simulate transient model node OOM on Dedicated capacity (trigger a capacity fallback to Hosted), causing the gateway to replay in-flight chunks without preserving original idempotency token.
3) Client SDK auto-retries previous chunk(s) on network error leading to duplicate requests and KV cache invalidation; observe increased 5xx rate and client-side retransmissions.
4) Observe request traces showing repeated dispatch of same logical request across different backends and rising request queue lengths.
5) Reproduce locally with a tenant-configured synthetic load generator that ramps multipart chunk loss and rapid fallback between backends.
impact: High — multiple paying customers experienced degraded streaming availability and higher error budgets; some teams reported user-facing session drops and support escalations with priority escalations to SRE and account teams.
mitigation: 1) Deploy adaptive retry-suppression gate at the edge: when backend return 5xx rate for tenant exceeds threshold, drop client-side auto-retries for idempotency-missing requests and return 429 with recommended client backoff. 2) Soft-quarantine affected tenant to Dedicated->Hosted fallback hysteresis window (60s) to avoid rapid flip-flop. 3) Enable temporary sampling for full request bodies for faster root-cause traces.
root_cause_summary: The gateway replay path failed to preserve the client-provided idempotency header for multipart/streaming chunks during cross-mode fallback. SDKs without explicit idempotency tokens emitted ephemeral tokens per chunk; when the gateway retried chunks due to backend transient errors, duplicate logical writes were observed causing downstream model runtime KV cache churn and series of 5xx errors. Additionally, aggressive client-side retries amplified the effect.
proposed_solution: Short term: edge adaptive retry-suppression and tenant hysteresis (implemented as feature flag). Medium term: normalize idempotency at gateway -> require/propagate X-Redwood-Idempotency or convert ephemeral tokens to canonical session token during session establishment. Long term: SDK change to expose session token and console guidance + automatic SDK patch release.
acceptance_criteria: Edge feature flag deployed to canary region and validated to reduce duplicate logical requests under synthetic loss test by >= 90%.
Per-tenant quarantine hysteresis prevents flip-flop between Dedicated and Hosted for at least 60s under injected node failures.
Telemetry dashboards added showing idempotency-header presence rate, duplicate-request ratio, and tenant-level fallback count; new alerts for duplicate-request ratio > 1%.
SDK patch submitted and smoke-tested: SDK can opt-in to session token generation; documentation updated.
timeline: 2026-03-01 — Customer A reported repeated streaming session drops and sent trace bundle. Triage assigned to oncall SRE and Platform PM.
2026-03-02 — Reproduced locally: observed gateway replay without idempotency header; created temporary sampling build. Shared initial findings in #sre and #platform-runtime.

2026-03-03 — Emergency mitigation prototyped: adaptive retry-suppression gate at edge returns 429 for requests missing X-Redwood-Idempotency when tenant 5xx rate > threshold. Deployed to us-west-2 canary. Noted reduction in duplicate dispatch volume on canary traffic.

2026-03-04 — Customer escalation call with Customer A and B. Comms team drafted interim guidance: ask customers to upgrade SDK to opt-in session token or apply client-side backoff. PM created customer-facing status update template.
2026-03-05 — Observed one false-positive where legitimate intermittent packet loss caused user-visible 429s; adjusted threshold and added a 10s grace window to avoid aggressive suppression.
2026-03-06 — Implemented soft-quarantine hysteresis between Dedicated and Hosted with 60s cooldown. Deployed to canary and rolled to 25% of production traffic after smoke tests.
2026-03-08 — Added telemetry: duplicate-request ratio and idempotency header presence to runtime dashboards. Pager alert configured for duplicate-request ratio > 0.5% sustained 5m.
2026-03-09 — Drafted SDK change and opened RFC for session token handshake between SDK and gateway. Code owner review requested. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4582

2026-03-10 — Started integration tests with Dedicated fallback harness and synthetic streaming-loss generator. Early results: duplicate-request rate reduced 85% with adaptive suppression + hysteresis.
2026-03-11 — This ticket split: short-term mitigation tracked here; follow-up tickets created for SDK release and gateway idempotency normalization (ENG-421421, ENG-421422).
